key_insight: DatBench defines and operationalizes three core desiderata for vision–language model (VLM) evaluation — faithfulness to modality/application, discriminability between model qualities, and compute efficiency — producing an evaluation suite that more reliably distinguishes real model differences while saving resources.
problem_solved: Current VLM evaluations are inconsistent: they often fail to reflect real-world multimodal tasks (lack faithfulness), cannot clearly separate stronger from weaker models (low discriminability), and are costly to run (inefficient). DatBench addresses all three simultaneously.
method: Formalize three evaluation desiderata (faithfulness, discriminability, efficiency) and derive measurable criteria for each.
Curate modality-aligned tasks and controlled protocols that emphasize real application behaviors and maximize signal between models (e.g., targeted probes, contrastive task designs).
Optimize the evaluation pipeline for compute (adaptive sampling, lightweight probes, aggregated scoring) to deliver reliable comparisons with lower resource cost.
impact: Provides practitioners and researchers a principled, resource-conscious way to compare VLMs that better reflects real-world performance and uncovers meaningful model differences, accelerating trustworthy selection and iteration.

paper_title: DatBench: Discriminative, Faithful, and Efficient VLM Evaluations
paper_authors: Siddharth Joshi, Haoli Yin, Rishabh Adiga, Ricardo Monti, Aldo Carranza
